lines.japanese: 「でもさ、渡来さんに作業を手伝ってもらえるのはありがたいんだけど、受験勉強とかは平気？」
lines.english: “I really appreciate you helping me with all this, Watarai, but... are you sure you have time? What about studying for entrance exams?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「その、余計なことかもしれないけど……」
lines.english: “I mean, it may be none of my business...”

lines.japanese: 僕は俯きながら聞いてみた。渡来さんには手伝って欲しいのが本音だ。でも受験生にとって、いまはとても大事な時期のはず。決して無視できない問題だ。
lines.english: I asked with my head bowed. The truth was, I wanted her help. But this had to be a crucial time for anyone facing entrance exams. I couldn’t simply ignore that.

lines.japanese: 「アそっか、まだ言ってなかったっけ。私はもう進路決まってるんだよね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Did I never tell you? My plans are already settled.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そうなの？」
lines.english: “Oh, really?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。進学希望だったけど、推薦で１１月にはとっくに。だからみんなには申し訳ないけど、ある程度余裕を持って学校生活を楽しんでるよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. I wanted to go to college, and I got in through a recommendation way back in November. I feel bad for everyone else, but I’ve got enough breathing room to enjoy what’s left of school.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。ああ、もしかして？　時間に余裕が出来たから、ゲームをやろうと思ったの？」
lines.english: “I see. Wait—is that why you decided to try the game? Because you had time on your hands?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　んー……あ、うんうん。そんな感じ。羽田君は？」
lines.english: “Hm? Well... oh, yeah. Something like that. What about you, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「え、おれ？　ああ受験？」
lines.english: “Me? Oh, the exams?”

lines.japanese: 僕は三年生の始めに進学希望と答えたから、形式的には受験生という扱いになってる。
lines.english: At the beginning of my third year, I had said I intended to continue my education. On paper, that made me another college applicant.

lines.japanese: だけどいずれグレタガルドへ戻る僕にとって受験勉強なんて、みんながしてるから目立たないようになんとなく合わせてる程度のものでしかない。
lines.english: But I would be returning to Gretagard eventually. Entrance-exam study was nothing more than an effort to follow everyone else’s lead and keep from standing out.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君って受験生のわりにあんまり焦ってる感じしないもんね。立場は違えど、相談になら乗るよ？　それとももう、焦るまでもなく余裕ってやつ？」
lines.english: “You never seem very nervous for somebody taking entrance exams. We’re in different situations, but I’m happy to give you advice. Unless you’re so sure of yourself you don’t need to worry?”

lines.japanese: 「ん……うん」
lines.english: “Mm... yeah.”

lines.japanese: 僕は曖昧な返事で頷いた。
lines.english: I nodded and gave a vague answer.

lines.japanese: 最近になって僕は、ときおり「向こうの現実」を遠いものに感じていた。本当に戻る日は来るんだろうか。グレタガルドは僕を受けいれるんだろうか。
lines.english: Lately, that “other reality” had sometimes begun to feel very far away. Would the day truly come when I returned? Would Gretagard take me back?

lines.japanese: もし駄目だったら、もし卒業後もこの世界で続けていくとしたら、はたして四ヵ月後の僕はどうしているんだろう。
lines.english: What if it did not? If I had to go on living in this world after graduation, what would I be doing four months from now?

lines.japanese: 不安が影をもたげる。ちょっと前までは、来年のことなんて考えなくてよかったのに。
lines.english: Anxiety stirred in the shadows. Until only recently, I had never needed to think about next year at all.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんはどこに行くの」
lines.english: “Where are you going, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　大学？」
lines.english: “Hm? For college?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん、参考までにね。もし教えてもらえればと思ってさ」
lines.english: “Yeah. Just as a point of reference, if you don’t mind telling me.”

lines.japanese: 「参考って？　私と同じトコに行きたいとか、あはは」
lines.english: “Reference for what? Thinking of going to the same place as me? Ahaha.”

lines.japanese: 僕はその問いかけに戸惑った。渡来さんとさわやかキャンパスライフ。そんな空想が頭をよぎる。
lines.english: The question caught me off guard. A bright and breezy college life with Watarai. The fantasy flitted through my head.
“Yeah...”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「どうせ進学するなら、それもいいかなって……」
lines.english: “If I’m going to college anyway... I thought that might be nice.”

lines.japanese: 「お、ヨユーの発言。羽田君はそんなに自信があるんだ」
lines.english: “Ooh, confident. You’re that sure you can get in, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、ないよそんなの」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Not at all.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、今から頑張って……」
lines.english: “But if I started working now...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、頑張れば、もしかしたら……なんとかなるかもしれないし……」
lines.english: “Yeah. If I worked hard, then maybe... maybe I could make it somehow...”

lines.japanese: 自分でも驚きの発言。なんとかなるかもで、いい加減に進学先なんて決めるもんじゃない。だけど今の僕にとってそれは、進路を決する理由として充分なものだった。
lines.english: I could hardly believe I had said it. ‘Maybe I could make it’ was no way to pick a college on a whim. Yet at that moment, it felt like reason enough to choose the course of my life.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんと同じ学校。
lines.english: The same school as Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「うん、なるほどだ」
lines.english: “Mm. I see how it is.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは作業の手を止めて、小さく微笑んでくれた。
lines.english: Watarai stopped working and gave me a small smile.

lines.japanese: 「私が使ってた参考書、羽田君にあげるよ」
lines.english: “I’ll give you the study guides I used.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「案内も持ってきた方がいいよね。今度持ってくる」
lines.english: “I should bring the school guide too, shouldn’t I? I’ll bring it next time.”

lines.japanese: 「え、い、いいよそんな。わざわざ悪いじゃん」
lines.english: “N-no, you don’t have to do all that. I’d feel bad making you go to the trouble.”

lines.japanese: 「本気でやるなら遠慮なんてしなくていいの。使えるものは全部使う。はいこれ、受験生の基本姿勢」
lines.english: “If you’re serious, don’t stand on ceremony. Use everything you can get. There—the cardinal rule of the college applicant.”

lines.japanese: ねえ渡来さん。それは僕ともう四年一緒にいたいってことなのかな？
lines.english: Tell me, Watarai. Did that mean you wanted four more years with me?

lines.japanese: 頭には浮かんだけど、それを口に出来るほどの勇気が今の僕にはなかった。
lines.english: The thought came to me. I did not yet have the courage to give it voice.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう……おれ、がんばるよ」
lines.english: “Thank you... I'll work hard.”

lines.japanese: 代わりに口にしたのは、小学生みたいな決意表明。
lines.english: What came out instead was the kind of solemn little vow a grade-schooler might make.

lines.japanese: 「こらこら、こんなとこでウル目になってちゃ駄目だよ。それは受かってからにするべきだよね」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, no misty eyes yet. You’re supposed to save that for after you get in.”

lines.japanese: 「ウル目になんてなってないよ。失礼なこと言わないでよ」
lines.english: “My eyes aren’t misty. Don’t say things like that.”

lines.japanese: 「えー？　ちょっと目を見せてみろ。あ、こら、逃げるな」
lines.english: “Oh, really? Let me see your eyes. Hey—quit running away.”

lines.japanese: 「逃げてないよ、ちょっと目にゴミが入ったんだよ」
lines.english: “I’m not running. I got something in my eye.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ確かめてあげるからこっち見てよ」
lines.english: “Then look at me and I’ll check.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで指をチョキ型にして構えてるんだよ。しかも顔がいやらしいよ、明らかになにか企んでる笑みだろ、それー」
lines.english: “Why are you coming at me with two fingers like scissors? And what’s with that sinister look? You’re obviously plotting something—that grin gives you away!”

lines.japanese: 「人聞きの悪いことを言わない。人聞きっていうか、私と羽田君しかいないけどね」
lines.english: “Don’t make me sound like a creep. Though I suppose there’s no one here to hear it but you and me.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、二人っきり……」
lines.english: “Yeah. Just the two of us...”

lines.japanese: しばらく無言の間があった。
lines.english: For a while, neither of us spoke.

lines.japanese: いままでの僕は、会話の合間合間に立ちあがってくる沈黙を息苦しいものに感じていた。だけどこんなに安らぐ静寂もあったんだ。
lines.english: Until now, I had always found the silences that rose in the gaps between words suffocating. I had never known silence could be this peaceful.

lines.japanese: 感謝の言葉、他愛のない冗談、なんだか温かくて手放したくない気持ち。いろんなことが頭に浮かんだけど、口にしなくても渡来さんにはぜんぶ伝わってる気がした──
lines.english: Words of thanks. Silly jokes. A warmth I never wanted to let go. So many things passed through my mind, yet I felt Watarai understood them all without my saying a word—

lines.japanese: ──なんて、ちょっと図々しいか。
lines.english: —though perhaps that was a little presumptuous of me.

lines.japanese: 「どした、黙っちゃって」
lines.english: “What’s wrong? Gone all quiet.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんこそ」
lines.english: “So have you.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだか静かな教室で作業するのも楽しいなって思って」
lines.english: “I was just thinking it’s kind of nice, working together in a quiet classroom.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「へへ」
lines.english: “Hehe.”

lines.japanese: 僕はどんな受け答えをすればいいんだろう。次の言葉が出てこない。
lines.english: How was I supposed to answer that? The next words would not come.

lines.japanese: 「ええと……」
飾らないでいい。いま一番に伝えたいこと。いまこの瞬間に思ったこと。渡来さんの笑顔はとても素敵だから、それをそのまま口にすればいいんだ。
lines.english: I did not need to dress it up. I only had to tell her the thing I most wanted her to know—the thing I felt in this very instant. Watarai’s smile was beautiful. All I had to do was say so.

lines.japanese: 正面から彼女の目を見つめる。それはとても簡単なことだった。
lines.english: I looked her straight in the eyes. It was the easiest thing in the world.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんの──」
lines.english: “Watarai, your—”

lines.japanese: ガチャッ
lines.english: Clack.

lines.japanese: 教室のドアが開いた。なぜだか僕は慌てて、原稿用紙をとんとん揃えていた。
lines.english: The classroom door opened. For some reason, I panicked and began tapping the manuscript pages into a neat stack.

lines.japanese: 「あ、先輩」
lines.english: “Oh, Hariu.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんだった。
lines.english: It was Hariu.

lines.japanese: 「なにしてたの？」
lines.english: “What were you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに。職員室で進展のない話をしてた」
lines.english: “Nothing. Having another conversation in the faculty room that went nowhere.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはまっすぐ自分の机へ向かい、脇にかかっていた鞄を掴むとすぐに体を翻す。億劫そうだけど不思議と引きしまって見える、綺麗な動きだった。
lines.english: Hariu went straight to his desk, took the bag hanging beside it, and wheeled around. It looked almost languid, yet somehow taut and graceful—a beautiful motion.

lines.japanese: あ、いや、ボーッと見てる場合じゃない。今日も卒文製作に誘わないと……。
lines.english: No, this was no time to stand there staring. I had to ask him to help with the graduation anthology again today...

lines.japanese: 「先輩手伝ってよ」
lines.english: “Help us out, Hariu.”

lines.japanese: 僕より早く渡来さんが声をかけてくれた。針生さんが少しだけこちらに首を向ける。
lines.english: Watarai beat me to it. Hariu turned his head slightly in our direction.

lines.japanese: 「断る」
lines.english: “Pass.”

lines.japanese: だけど答えは僕らを突きはなした。
lines.english: The answer shoved us away.

lines.japanese: 「どうせ暇じゃん」
lines.english: “You're not doing anything anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「ふン」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは薄笑いを浮かべると、渡来さんではなく僕を一瞥した。
lines.english: Hariu gave a thin smile, then glanced at me rather than Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「あ、暇じゃないですよね。仏像のことがありますもんね」
lines.english: “Oh, right—you’re not free. You’ve got your Buddhist statues to think about.”

lines.japanese: 「仏像かあ。そんなトキもあったなァ」
lines.english: “Buddhist statues, huh. I remember when I was into those.”

lines.japanese: 「おれもいろいろ調べてみたんですけど、この近くに一木造りの仏像があって――」
lines.english: “I did some research too, actually. There’s a single-block wooden statue near here—”

lines.japanese: 「今はこれだろ」
lines.english: “This is where it’s at now.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは片手を上げて僕の言葉を制した。鞄の中から双眼鏡を取りだしてみせる。
lines.english: Hariu raised one hand to cut me off, then produced a pair of binoculars from his bag.

lines.japanese: 「いま野鳥にハマッてるんだ。悪いけどそれどころじゃない」
lines.english: “I’m into wild birds now. Sorry, but I don’t have time for anything else.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、バードウォッチングとかって面白いですよね。おれも一時期ハマりかけたんです」
lines.english: “Bird-watching is fascinating, isn’t it? I nearly got hooked on it myself once.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはどうやら多趣味なひとみたいだ。でも今回、僕にも造詣のある分野だったことはラッキーだ。よし、今日こそ針生さんと語りあってみよう。
lines.english: Hariu seemed to be a man of many interests. This time, though, luck had landed him in a field I knew something about. All right. Today I would finally manage a real conversation with him.

lines.japanese: 「シジュウカラとヤマガラの鳴き声の見分け方なんですけどね、便利な方法があるんですよ。まず、シジュウカラの鳴き声のツーツーって声に……」
lines.english: “There’s a handy way to tell a Japanese tit’s call from a varied tit’s. First, take the tee-tee of the Japanese tit...”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、野鳥に興味があるんだ」
lines.english: “Oh? You're interested in wild birds?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんが体を向けてくれた。よかった、これでいっぱい話ができるかもしれない。
lines.english: Hariu turned to face me. Good. Maybe now we could talk for a good long while.

lines.japanese: 「それなら今週末に俺が連れていってやるから、島に行くぞ。ひとりで行こうと思ってたけど、まあ今回だけは人がいても構わない。渡り鳥が集まるいい離島があるんだ」
lines.english: “Then I’ll take you this weekend. We’re going to an island. I meant to go alone, but I suppose company won’t hurt just this once. I know a good little island where migratory birds gather.”

lines.japanese: 「天候によっては一週間くらい帰れなくなるかもしれないけれど、それも一興だろ。んじゃ、待ちあわせについて――」
lines.english: “Depending on the weather, we might not make it back for a week or so. That’s half the fun. Now, about where to meet—”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、すみません……週末は妹と大掃除をしようと思ってるんです」
lines.english: “Um, I’m sorry... I was planning to give the house a thorough cleaning with my sister this weekend.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか。じゃあな」
lines.english: “I see. Later.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはあっさり出ていってしまった。残念だけどまた次の機会に話しかけてみよう。今後会ったときはどんな趣味に目覚めているのかな。ちょっと楽しみだった。
lines.english: Hariu left without a second thought. It was a shame, but I could always try talking to him next time. What new hobby would have seized him by then? I found myself looking forward to it a little.

lines.japanese: 「まったく先輩は、暇人のくせに偉そうだよね」
lines.english: “Honestly, Hariu acts so high and mighty for someone with nothing to do.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは針生さんの出ていったドアに文句をぶつけている。でもそれは決して敵意や悪意が込められたものではなく、ごく親しい者へのみ向ける諧謔のようだった。
lines.english: Watarai flung the complaint at the door Hariu had gone through. Yet there was no hostility or malice in it—only the teasing one reserves for someone very close.

lines.japanese: たとえば恋人に向けるような。
lines.english: For a lover, perhaps.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ」
僕は尋ねかけて──
lines.english: I began to ask—

lines.japanese: 「や、なんでもない」
lines.english: “No, never mind.”

lines.japanese: ──やめた。そんなことを聞いて誰が得をするっていうんだ。
lines.english: —and stopped. Who could possibly benefit from my asking a question like that?
“What? What is it?”

lines.japanese: なんだろう。気付いたら渡来さんが白けた顔で僕を眺めていた。
lines.english: What was this? At some point, Watarai had begun staring at me with a thoroughly unimpressed look.

lines.japanese: 「言いたいことがあるならちゃんと言いなさい」
lines.english: “If you have something to say, say it properly.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、まあ、そんなどうしても聞きたいわけじゃないんだけどさ」
lines.english: “Well, it’s not like I absolutely have to know or anything...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、何でも聞いて」
lines.english: “Go ahead. Ask me anything.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんって、針生さんと仲いいよね。いや、まあ、気になるわけじゃないんだけどさ」
lines.english: “You and Hariu are close, aren’t you? Not that I’m bothered by it or anything.”

lines.japanese: ないんだけど、渡来さんが何でも聞いてって言うから聞いてみたんだ。そう、それだ。
lines.english: I wasn’t. I had only asked because Watarai said I could ask her anything. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あー、あー」
lines.english: “Ah, ah, ah.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんの頭がかくんかくんと右へ三回傾いた。
lines.english: Watarai’s head ticked three times to the right.

lines.japanese: 「前の学校同じ」
lines.english: “Same school before.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「ソラ学に入る前も同じ学校だったんだよ。彼が先輩で、私と顔見知り」
lines.english: “We went to the same school before Sora Academy too. He was in a higher grade, and we knew each other.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ……地元、同じなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh... You’re from the same area, then.”

lines.japanese: たしか渡来さんって、ここの入学に合わせて隣りの県から引っ越してきたんだった。
lines.english: If I remembered correctly, Watarai had moved here from the neighboring prefecture when she enrolled.

lines.japanese: 「面識あれば、自然とソラ学入っても顔合わせるでしょ？　しかも、同じクラスになるなんて思わないよね」
lines.english: “Once you already know somebody, of course you end up seeing each other at Sora, right? Though you never expect to land in the same class.”

lines.japanese: うん、たしかに上級生だったひとと同じクラスになるなんて、あんまり思わないだろう。
lines.english: True. You would hardly expect someone who used to be in a higher grade to wind up as your classmate.

lines.japanese: 「最初は微妙だけど、慣れてくるとお互いに、あーとか、おーって感じになるよね。うん、今もそんな感じかな」
lines.english: “It’s a little awkward at first, but once you get used to it, you’re both just like, ‘Oh,’ or ‘Hey.’ Yeah. That’s still about where we are.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだったんだ。あ、いや、気にしてたわけじゃないけどね。うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “I see. Not that I was worried about it or anything. Yeah. Sounds normal.”

lines.japanese: 僕は安心したような顔を見られるのが嫌で、教室の隅のごみ箱まで紙くずを捨てに行った。
lines.english: I did not want her to see the relief on my face, so I carried a scrap of paper all the way to the trash can in the corner.

lines.japanese: そうか、地元の先輩後輩か。なんだ、それだけなんだ。
lines.english: So that was it: he was only her old upperclassman from back home. Nothing more.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん、手伝ってくれるといいね」
lines.english: “I hope Hariu agrees to help.”

lines.japanese: もとの席へ戻って座りながら言った。
lines.english: I said it as I returned to my seat.

lines.japanese: 「あと山科さんもね」
lines.english: “Yamashina too.”

lines.japanese: 「また山科か」
lines.english: “Yamashina again.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　またって？」
lines.english: “What do you mean, again?”

lines.japanese: 「なんか最近よく話に出てくるなーと思って」
lines.english: “I was just thinking you’ve been bringing her up a lot lately.”

lines.japanese: 「そう？」
lines.english: “Have I?”

lines.japanese: 最近なんて言われたって、そもそも僕と渡来さんが話をするようになったこと自体が最近だ。
lines.english: She said lately, but Watarai and I had only started talking at all lately.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、だって同じ班だから気になるじゃない。病気っていうか、ほら体調も心配だし、友達としては」
lines.english: “Well, we’re in the same group, so of course I wonder about her. And she’s sick—or, well, I worry about her health. As a friend.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君と山科って仲良かったんだ。教室で話してるところなんて見たことなかったよ？」
lines.english: “I didn’t know you and Yamashina were close. I’ve never once seen you talk in class.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、最近になって話すようになったんだ。おれ友達少ないから、実はちょっと嬉しくてさ」
lines.english: “We only started talking recently. I don’t have many friends, so honestly, I’m kind of happy about it.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは顎に手を当てると、むっつり引きむすんだ唇を……あ、あれ？　さっきまでフツーに笑ってた気がするんだけど、いつの間にあんな表情になってたんだろう。
lines.english: Watarai put a hand to her chin, her lips pressed into a sullen line... Wait. I could have sworn she was smiling normally a moment ago. When had that expression appeared?

lines.japanese: 「なるほど……それで君は、山科のことが少し気になっていると」
lines.english: “I see... So Yamashina has been on your mind.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: なんだか下世話な言葉が出てきた。
lines.english: That was an awfully suggestive way to put it.

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、気になるとか、そういう言い方するようなアレじゃないけどさ……」
lines.english: “N-no, I wouldn’t say she’s ‘on my mind’ like that...”

lines.japanese: 「浮気？」
lines.english: “Cheating?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「浮気だよね」
lines.english: “You’re cheating on me, aren’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ、なんだよそれ、浮気も何も……」
lines.english: “What are you talking about? How could it be cheating when...”

lines.japanese: 僕たち形だけの恋人じゃないか。一瞬そう反論しかけたけど呑みこんだ。
lines.english: We were only pretending to be lovers. For an instant I nearly said so, but swallowed the words.

lines.japanese: それを口にしたが最後、この楽しい恋人ごっこが時間ごと氷りついて終わってしまいそうだったから。
lines.english: The moment I said it aloud, this happy game of lovers might freeze over—time and all—and come to an end.

lines.japanese: だから僕らは、おままごと遊びの夫婦を演じる子供みたいに、無邪気な笑みを絶やさなかった。
lines.english: And so, like children playing house as husband and wife, we never let our innocent smiles slip.

lines.japanese: 「浮気って言っちゃいなよ」
lines.english: “Come on. Say you’re cheating.”

lines.japanese: 「してないって。してないってば、そんなこと」
lines.english: “I’m not. I told you, I’m not doing anything like that.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、私の目を見て言ってごらん」
lines.english: “Look me in the eye and say it, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、いいよ」
lines.english: “A-all right. Fine.”

lines.japanese: まっすぐ渡来さんの正面に向きあうと、少女漫画みたいな瞳が飛びこんできた。
lines.english: I turned squarely toward her, and a pair of eyes straight out of a romance manga leaped into view.

lines.japanese: きらきらまんまるな目に当てられて、僕は２秒で目を逸らした。
lines.english: Those great, round, sparkling eyes hit me full force. I looked away in two seconds.

lines.japanese: 「そこで逸らすかフツー」
lines.english: “Who looks away there? Seriously.”

lines.japanese: 「べつに悪いことなんてしてないよ」
lines.english: “I haven’t done anything wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「だから私の目を見なさい」
lines.english: “Then look me in the eye.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いいよ」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 「は、羽田君が私と目を合わせてくれない」
lines.english: “H-Haneda won’t look me in the eye.”

lines.japanese: こうして残りの時間、僕はひたすら作業に集中することができた。おかげで高内さんに頼まれた仕事もやっつけることができた。
lines.english: That was how I managed to devote the rest of our time entirely to work. Thanks to that, I even polished off the job Takauchi had given me.

lines.japanese: うーん、今日は働いたって感じだなあ。
lines.english: Mm. Now that felt like an honest day’s work.

lines.japanese: 「ねえねえ羽田君、私は浮気が嫌いだよ。絶対に許さない派だよ。どんな理由でも認めないよ」
lines.english: “Listen, Haneda. I hate cheaters. I’m in the never, ever forgive them camp. I don’t care what the excuse is.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはまだ夫婦ごっこを続けていた。
lines.english: Watarai was still playing at married life.

lines.japanese: 「浮気したら本気でグーパンしてやる」
lines.english: “If you ever cheat on me, I’ll seriously deck you.”

lines.japanese: ごっこ……だよね？
lines.english: We were... playing, right?
